title: PCR-based assay for genotyping of the slick mutation in cattle
author: Elizabeth Jannaman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6kxhcxn

Laboratory Procedures, PJ Hansen Laboratory - University of Florida 1 | Slick mutation KASP genotyping assay PCR-based assay for genotyping of the slick mutation in cattle Elizabeth Jannaman1, M Sofia Ortega2, Tad S Sonstegard3, and Peter J Hansen1 1Department of Animal Sciences, University of Florida 2Division of Animal Sciences, University of Missouri 3Recombinetics, Inc., Saint Paul, Minnesota Introduction Several mutations exist in the prolactin receptor gene (PRLR) o f cattle that cause a short, sleek hair coat (Porto-Neto et al., 2018). The mutation is dominant so sl ick-haired cattle can have either one or two copies of the mutation. The assay described here detects the most-well studied mutation (SLICK1) that causes translation of a truncated PRLR of 461 amino acids. Originally described in Senepol cattle, this mutation has also been introduced into Holsteins in Puerto Rico, Florida and elsewhere. Note that the assay will not detect other mutations in PRLR that also cause the slick phenotype. Part 1: DNA Extraction DNA is extracted from whole blood samples (fresh or previously frozen at -20°C) using Thermo Fisher’s PureLink Genomic DNA Mini Kit (cat# K182001). For additional pr oduct details, alternate procedures (i.e., for cells), and troubleshooting refer to the product manual which can be found on the ThermoFisher website at https://www.thermofisher.com/document-connect/document-connect.html?url=https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-
Assets/LSG/manuals/purelink_genomic_man.pdf Note that there are more inexpensive methods of DNA extraction available. The method below is used because of its simplicity and speed. Materials & Supplies Needed Pure Link Genomic DNA Mini Kit 96-100% Ethanol (Sigma cat# E7023) Water bath set to 55⁰C Sterile 2 mL snap cap tubes – 2 per sample (Corning Costar microcentrifuge tubes, Fisher cat# 3213) Microcentrifuge Pipettors and sterile pipette tips

Laboratory Procedures, PJ Hansen Laboratory - University of Florida 3 | Slick mutation KASP genotyping assay Part 2: PCR Materials KASP Assay primer (Cat #KBS-2100-100 LGC Genomics) Primer ID: Indel 1 Primer Allele 5’-FAM GGACCAAACAGACCAACATGC-3’ (wild-type allele) Primer Allele 5’-HEX CTGGACCAAACAGACCAACATGT-3’ (slick allele) Primer Common 5’-CCTTCCCTGCCAGTTTCAATGGTTT-3’ KASP V4.0 2x Master Mix (cat #KBS-1016-002-US LGC Genomics) RNAse free water (Cat# 1017979 Qiagen) 96 well PCR plates (Cat#MLL9601 Bio-Rad) Micro seal ‘B’ seals (Cat#MSB1001 Bio-Rad) Individual 0.2 µL PCR tubes (Cat#TFI10201 Bio-Rad) Pipettors and sterile pipette tips Plate centrifuge Procedure Plate Setup & Loading 1. Normalize the DNA samples to a final concentration of 10 ng/µL using RNase free water to dilute samples. 2. Prepare master mix stock in s terile tube; (5 µL KASP Master Mix + 0.14 µL KASP Primer Indel 1) X # reactions a. Add an extra 2-5 reactions to the calculations to allow for pipetting error. 3. Prepare a plate layout diagram with samples. All samples should be run in duplicate. 4. Add 5 µL master mix stock so lution to each well that will be used in the 96 well plate. 5. Following plate layout diagr am, add 5 µL of each diluted DNA sample to the corresponding well. a. Gently mix or vortex sam ple to ensure uniformity. b. Change pipette tips between each well. 6. Cover plate with seal tightly , ensuring no edges are lifted. a. Tip: use the blunt end of a m arker to run along junctions of the plate to ensure a tight seal. 7. Centrifuge plate for ~30 sec to ensure samples are at the bottom of each well.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary buffers and equipment for the DNA extraction process.

substeps.instruction: Add ethanol to Wash Buffer 1 and Wash Buffer 2 as described on the label (if not already completed).
Set water bath to 55 ⁰C.
Vortex all solutions to dissolve any precipitate present.

steps.title: Lysis and Protein Digestion
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from the whole blood sample using a lysis and digestion process.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL whole blood to a sterile microcentrifuge tube labeled with sample ID.
Add 20 µL Proteinase K to the sample.
Add 200 µL Lysis/Binding Buffer and vortex for 5 seconds to obtain a homogenous solution.
Incubate in the 55 ⁰C water bath for 10 minutes to promote protein digestion.
Add 200 µL ethanol to the lysate and vortex for 5 seconds to obtain a homogenous solution.

steps.title: DNA Binding and Washing
steps.instruction: Purify the DNA using a PureLink spin column and wash buffers.

substeps.instruction: Pipette the entire volume of lysate (~640 µL) into a labeled PureLink spin column.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 10,000 x g at room temperature.
Discard the collection tube and place the spin column into a new clean collection tube from the kit.
Add 500 µL Wash Buffer 1 to the spin column.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 10,000 x g at room temperature.
Discard the collection tube and place the spin column into a new clean collection tube from the kit.
Add 500 µL Wash Buffer 2 to the spin column.
Centrifuge for 3 minutes at maximum speed (~21,000 x g) at room temperature.

steps.title: DNA Elution
steps.instruction: Elute the purified DNA into a sterile tube for PCR use.

substeps.instruction: Discard the collection tube and place the spin column into a sterile 2 mL microcentrifuge tube labeled with sample ID.
Add 50 µL of Genomic Elution Buffer to the spin column (refer to manufacturer's handbook pg 13 for volume guidelines).
Incubate for 1 minute at room temperature.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at maximum speed (~21,000 x g) at room temperature with the 2 mL tube top open, pointing to the side or bottom of the centrifuge.
Remove and discard the spin column; purified DNA is now in the bottom of the 2 mL tube.
Optional: Perform a second elution in an additional 2 mL microcentrifuge tube if more DNA is desired.

steps.title: Configure CFX Manager Software
steps.instruction: Set up the KASP assay protocol and plate layout in the CFX Manager program.

substeps.instruction: Open CFX Manager program and Create New Run.

Create and save the KASP assay protocol with the following parameters: 1) 94.0 C for 15:00; 2) 94.0 C for 0:20; 3) 61.0 C for 1:00 with a decrement of -0.6 C per cycle; 4) Repeat steps 2-3 for 9 more cycles; 5) 94.0 C for 0:20; 6) 55.0 C for 1:00; 7) Repeat steps 5-6 for 25 more cycles; 8) 37.0 C for 1:00 + Plate Read.
Create and save a KASP assay plate layout where each well is assigned: Sample Type (NTC), LOAD FAM, HEX, and ROX, and Sample Name (input sample ID).
Ensure each sample is run in duplicate.

steps.title: Run PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Load the samples into the PCR machine and execute the run.

substeps.instruction: Open the PCR machine using computer controls or the button (do not force the lid).
Load prepared plates into the PCR machine.
Close the PCR machine using computer controls or the button (do not force the lid).
Press START RUN (total run time is approximately 1.5 hours).

steps.title: Analyze Genotyping Results
steps.instruction: Interpret the Allelic Discrimination results from the CFX Manager screen.

substeps.instruction: Identify wild type (non-slick) animals by zero copies of the slick allele or two copies of the FAM allele (zero HEX).
Identify heterozygotes by one (1) copy of the HEX slick allele.
Identify homozygous animals by two (2) copies of the HEX slick allele.
Use controls of known genotypes (heterozygote and both homozygotes) to verify grouping and manually adjust result graph lines if necessary.
